summary: Strong bundle. Every HCS SL/RSS per diem, bill code, attendant/other-direct/indirect component, host home, nursing, behavioral support, ISS, respite, CFC, supported employment and non-state ICF/IID small-facility rate matches the HHSC PFD sheets (9/1/2025 HCS and ICF; 1/1/2025 HCS). 9/1/2025 is still the latest posted HCS rate sheet. The $13.00 wage and 15% residential PTB match IL 2025-17 (Rider 23); ACRE ending matches IL 2025-21. All O*NET/BLS 2025 Texas wages check out (aide median $11.65 / 75th $13.23; DFW $12.93 / $14.51; Austin $13.64; RN $46.14; LVN $29.92; SCSM $76,520; med sec $42,910). Zillow ZORI Aug 2026 (Dallas $2,371, Houston $2,242, Austin $2,312, San Antonio $1,845), the CY2026 Medicaid fee ($750, 90 FR 55738), TWC 2.70%/$9,000, the franchise no-tax-due threshold of $2,650,000, the SOS Form 205 fee of $300, SSI $994 and the interest list data (135,497; 483 enrolled; 128,110; 9,225 added/1,835 removed; 199,471 unduplicated) all verified. Rule citations (26 TAC 263.5, 263.106, 263.502, 263.601, 565.3, 565.7, 565.9, 565.13, 565.23, 565.27, 565.41, 565.43, 52.27-52.41, 52.103(g); 1 TAC 354.4005) say what the bundle claims, and the contacts (512-438-3161, LTCRPolicy, four-person residence email, 1-800-458-9858, IDD Ombudsman, CAPM fax/mail code) match HHSC documents. Recomputing the model reproduces every figure (hcs6_rss +$7,126, BE 0.885; hcs4_rss +$2,989, BE 0.902; hcs4_rss_lowlon +$2,544; hcs3_homes -$1,712; rss4_single -$1,924; sl3_single -$3,720) and the narrative sensitivities ($14.51 -> -$4,240; $15.00 -> -$6,586; owner PM +$10,450; full SSI +$5,130; no nursing +$1,700). Staffing meets the 263.5 rules for every RSS configuration (>=730 awake hours per home). No critical issues. Main fixes: the break-even DSP wage is about $13.62, not $13.40; HHSC has published exact FY2026 cost limits (IL 2025-21), so that not_claimed item should become a claim; the 3-person SL staffing depends on an unsourced 'residents away ~130 h/month' assumption; and there are a few source-id, URL and wording fixes.

issues.current: any DSP wage above roughly $13.40 erases the margin at current rates
issues.correct: any DSP wage above roughly $13.60 erases the margin at current rates
issues.evidence: Recomputed with generators/model.py: at a $13.40 wage the hcs4_rss default is still +$1,074/month. Each $1/hour raises costs about $4,790/month ((4,240+2,989)/1.51), so break-even is $13.00 + 2,989/4,790 ≈ $13.62.
issues.fix: Replace '$13.40' with '$13.60' (break-even DSP wage ≈ $13.62 for the default four-home configuration).

issues.current: Exact final HCS individual cost limit dollar amounts for FY2026 — HHSC set the method (210% of annualized ICF/IID cost by LON) [S6]; secondary estimates exist but were not verified against an HHSC publication.
issues.evidence: IL 2025-21, p.5: 'Intermittent (LON 1), Limited (LON 5), and Extensive (LON 8) — The amount is going from $167,468 to $169,182 ... Pervasive (LON 6): ... $168,615 to $211,822 ... Pervasive plus (LON 9): ... $305,877 to $392,318', each 210% of the annualized non-state small ICF/IID rate as of 9/1/2025. Check: $220.72 × 365 × 2.1 = $169,182.
issues.fix: Remove this not_claimed item. Add the three cost-limit amounts to key_numbers (source S5, as_of 2025-09-01) and to sections.reimbursement 'Payment limits' in place of 'below that kind of limit'.

issues.current: 637 h/month ... covers one staff member present whenever residents are home (24 h × 30.42 days minus ~130 weekday hours when residents attend individualized skills and socialization or work)
issues.evidence: 26 TAC §263.5(20) requires SL staff to be 'present in the residence and ... able to respond to the needs of individuals during normal sleeping hours'. The ~130 h/month that residents are assumed to be away (ISS or work) has no source. If residents are home all day, one-person coverage is 730 h. Recomputed sl3_single at 730 h: −$5,135/month (vs −$3,720), break-even occupancy 122%.
issues.fix: Label the ~130 h/month away from home 'operator estimate — verify locally (depends on residents' ISS/employment schedules)'. Add to financial_narrative: 'If residents are home all day (730 h), the 3-person SL home loses about $5,135/month.'

issues.current: Employer FICA 7.65% + Texas SUTA 2.70% on the first $9,000 for new employers + FUTA ≈ 8.5% of DSP payroll
issues.correct: ≈ 8.7% for a full-time DSP at $13.00 (FICA 7.65% + SUTA $243 + FUTA $42 on $27,040); higher for part-time or high-turnover staff earning under $9,000/year (up to 10.95%)
issues.evidence: TWC: '2026 ... entry-level rate is 2.70%'; taxable wage base $9,000. 2.7% × $9,000 = $243 plus FUTA 0.6% × $7,000 = $42, which is 1.05% of $27,040.
issues.fix: Change '≈ 8.5%' to '≈ 8.7% for a full-time DSP (more with part-time or turnover)'. The model total of 17% can stay.
